title: Confidence in Mexico Secures US Investment, Sheinbaum Says After Meeting With Business Leaders and Ambassador Johnson
author: Alma E. Muñoz and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by[Alma E. Muñoz and Alonso
Urrutia](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz%20y%20Alonso%20Urrutia)
originally appeared in the [October 8, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/08/politica/cce-destaca-
dialogo-constructivo-entre-sheinbaum-y-empresarios-de-estados-unidos),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. At the end of a meeting between U.S. business leaders—who
came accompanied by their ambassador, Ronald Johnson—and President Claudia
Sheinbaum, the president of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), José
Medina Mora, considered that it was a **very constructive dialogue** in which
each party had the opportunity to express its concerns and its purposes.

Through her social media, the President reported on the meeting at her
offices:

> We talked about the confidence in Mexico that secures the investment of U.S.
> companies and the importance of maintaining the trade relationship for the
> well-being of both countries.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

After noting that bilateral security actions were discussed, Medina Mora said
that the country has the most secure border in many years and that Mexico’s
efforts to prevent drug trafficking have reduced the flow of fentanyl to the
country to the north. Medina Mora considered that among the main concerns of
those attending was the need for the negotiations around the North American
trade agreement to finally be concluded successfully.

In an interview at the end of the meeting at the National Palace, Medina Mora
asserted that the ideal would be for the USMCA to be renewed for 16 more
years, but for now it will remain in force for ten years, with an annual
review of its terms. However, it needs to be ratified for 16 years with the
possibility of review every six years. This will allow **investment flows into
Mexico to increase** and, with that, the bilateral trade relationship to
continue growing.

Medina Mora said he trusts that the negotiations will make it possible to
reduce the tariffs imposed under Section 232 on the steel, aluminum and
vehicles that Mexico exports to the United States. He explained that this
meeting is a follow-up to the one held two years ago, at the dawn of
Sheinbaum’s government, with the American Chamber of Commerce of Mexico. He
highlighted that the U.S. business leaders left **satisfied because the
President listened to their concerns** so they can expand their investments in
Mexico.

For her part, the head of the Presidency’s Business Advisory Council,
Altagracia Gómez, reported that some investments to be made in various areas
were made known. She highlighted that investors attended with companies
specializing in pharmaceuticals, medical supplies, energy and others
associated with agriculture. She said that, without a doubt, some of them will
be able to formalize their announcement at an upcoming press conference.

Finally, she mentioned that on behalf of the Mexican government, those
attending included, among others, Secretary of the Economy Marcelo Ebrard,
Secretary of Foreign Affairs Roberto Velasco and Secretary of Energy Luz Elena
González.
